summary: Richard G. Salomon works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, having studied under Ludo Rocher. He served as a professor at the University of Washington (attested 1998–2017; professor emeritus attested 2026) and was a visiting researcher at Soka University in 2007.

Richard Schmidt was an Indologist who completed his doctorate under Richard Pischel and Karl Friedrich Geldner and his habilitation at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. He served there as Privatdozent (~1898–1906) and became ordinary professor at the University of Münster in 1910.
Richard Shilleto was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He was educated at Repton School, Shrewsbury School (~1823–1828), and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1828–1832).

Richard Sproat is a linguist in computational linguistics who studied at the University of California, San Diego, and MIT. He held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (2003–2009), Oregon Health and Science University (2009–2012), and Google (2012).

Richard Sylvan was a philosopher who studied at Victoria University of Wellington (~1953–1957) and Princeton University (~1957–1961). He held positions at the University of Sydney (~1963–1964) and the Australian National University (fellow, 1971).

Richard W. Lariviere is an Indologist who studied under Ludo Rocher at the University of Pennsylvania. He served as dean and professor emeritus at UT Austin, provost at the University of Kansas, president of the University of Oregon, and president of the Field Museum.

Richard Wilhelm was a Sinologist who studied at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium and the University of Tübingen (~1891–1895). He was a visiting professor at Peking University in 1923 and held the chair in Sinology at Goethe University Frankfurt starting in 1924.

Richard von Garbe was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Tübingen (Ph.D. under Rudolf von Roth) and Königsberg (habilitation). He held professorships at the University of Königsberg (1878–1880; 1894) and the University of Tübingen (1895–1927).

Richard von Glahn is a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. He held a professorship at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1987) and was a visiting fellow at the University of Tokyo (1988–1989).
Rigdzin Shikpo was a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under Chögyam Trungpa and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.

Riika J. Virtanen is a Tibetologist who completed doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki under supervisors Asko Parpola, Klaus Karttunen, and Hannu Riikonen, and also studied under Sangye Tandar Naga.
Rikizan Ishikawa was a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Komazawa University (~1962–1974) and served there as Professor of Buddhist Studies (~1991–1997).

Ringu Tulku is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Namgyal Institute, CIHTS, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. His teachers included Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Tubten Tsondru, and he taught at Naropa University.

Rinzin Thargyal was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology who completed his Magister degree at the University of Oslo in 1985, studying under supervisors Fredrik Barth and Arne Martin Klausen.

Rita Langer is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hamburg (supervised by Lambert Schmithausen) and studied at SOAS and PGIBS. She has held posts at the University of Bristol (attested 2009; 2026).

Rita M. Gross was a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her doctorate at the University of Chicago. She served as Professor Emerita at the University of Wisconsin–Eau Claire (~1973–1998) and taught at UW-Madison and Mindrolling Lotus Garden.
Ritu Birla is a historian and Indologist who studied at Columbia University (~1990–1996). She has served as Professor Emerita in the Department of History at the University of Toronto (~2001).

Rizong Sras Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who trained at Drepung Loseling Monastery (1950–1959). He studied under the 14th Dalai Lama, Losal Ling Khen Zur Jampal Sampel, and Pema Gyaltsen, and was abbot of Gyume, Drepung Loseling, and Samstanling.

Rob Linrothe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and history/archaeology who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago. He held faculty posts at Skidmore College (1992–2009) and Northwestern University (2010–2022).

Rob Nairn was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied law at the University of Zimbabwe, King's College London, Edinburgh, and London. He held professorial and lecturing posts at the University of Zimbabwe and the University of Cape Town.
